text.p: A Chrysler Corp spokesman said Wednesday that outside director John Neff purchased 50,000 shares of the automaker's common stock on April 15 for a total of $1.4 million.

The purchases were made at prices ranging between $28.63 and $28.88 during the 30-day window that Chrysler executives and directors can purchase shares following the company's quarterly earnings release.
Chrysler stock was trading at 31-3/4, up 1/4 on Wednesday.
Before the purchases, Neff was the beneficial owner of 33,944 shares of Chrysler's stock, according to the company's 1997 proxy statement.

Neff is a former managing director of Wellington Management Co, who managed the firm's Windsor Fund, a Chrysler shareholder. Chrysler named Neff to its board in February 1996 when the company was fending off takeover efforts by billionaire investor Kirk Kerkorian.
